items.title: Five days’ warning: New Malaysian model forecasts haze before it hits
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia will introduce several transformative measures to strengthen efforts to tackle transboundary haze when it chairs the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee (MSC) on Transboundary Haze Pollution next year. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said his ministry was conducting studies and drafting several new initiatives to ensure more effective and concrete action to address the recurring haze problem. “Malaysia will take over the MSC chairmanship next year, and we are studying and planning several new initiatives to strengthen Asean-level efforts to tackle the haze problem.

items.title: 29 foreigners held as police raid luxury bungalow, hotel scam hubs
items.summary: MELAKA TENGAH: Police have smashed two online scam syndicates operating out of a luxury bungalow and a hotel here, arresting 29 foreigners. The syndicates, which targeted victims in Vietnam and China, were crippled in separate raids by Melaka Tengah police. Melaka Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said the first raid on a two-storey bungalow in a resort area yesterday evening led to the arrest of 15 men aged between 21 and 40.

items.title: Son of Myanmar's Suu Kyi says had first call in five years
items.summary: YANGON: The son of Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi said Thursday he was allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years. "Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express," Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook.

items.title: No drones without approval, Melaka police tell election candidates
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 22 — Candidates and political parties intending to use drones during the Melaka State Election campaign must first obtain approval from the relevant authorities and cannot deploy the devices indiscriminately. Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said drone operations were subject to regulatory controls by the relevant authorities, including the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM). “Even the police must obtain approval before using drones for operational purposes,” he told reporters after attending a briefing on the 16th Melaka State Election for political party representatives at the Melaka Police Contingent Headquarters here today.

items.title: Snip, snip, slip through? Wire fences cut at illegal crossings near Rantau Panjang-Thai border
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 22 — Eleven police reports regarding damage to concertina wire fences at 13 illegal crossing points around Rantau Panjang were recorded between March 27 and October 12. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (PGA) Deputy Director Datuk Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said the damage was believed to have been deliberately done to open up pathways for smuggling activities and cross-border crimes. Suzrin said his team constantly updates field information alongside the National Security Council and the police contingent regarding fence-cutting incidents in the border areas.

items.title: Court grants Perikatan stay on RoS deregistration, allows coalition to contest Melaka state polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The High Court here today allowed Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) application to stay the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to revoke the coalition’s registration pending the outcome of its judicial review. Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad also granted PN’s application to stay the enforcement of an RoS notice suspending all activities of the political coalition. The decision allows PN to continue its political activities, including contesting the Melaka state election scheduled for November 14.

items.title: Evidence, sovereignty issues pose hurdles to transboundary haze law
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia faces major challenges in enacting transboundary haze pollution laws, particularly in obtaining evidence and addressing sovereignty issues that could undermine its enforcement. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the proposed legislation required comprehensive scrutiny, given the jurisdictional challenges involved in enforcement and its potential implications for diplomatic relations with other countries. The assessment must also consider the implications for diplomatic relations with regional countries and ensure the proposed legal framework could effectively address transboundary haze pollution, he added.

items.title: Malaysia demands effective action from Indonesia on transboundary haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia will demand effective action from Indonesia to tackle fires causing transboundary haze when it raises the issue at the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Manila early next month. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia respected its bilateral ties with Indonesia but had the right to demand measures to protect Malaysians' health and well-being. "We respect our good relations with Indonesia, but we also have the right to demand effective action when transboundary pollution affects our people.

items.title: Iran warns it will hit US bases if Hormuz ship escorts continue
items.summary: TEHRAN, Oct 22 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.

items.title: Canada's Carney visits Turkiye in push to ease US trade dependence
items.summary: ANKARA: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney will meet President Tayyip Erdogan in Turkiye on Thursday, in the first bilateral visit by a Canadian leader, as he seeks to expand trade ties and reduce reliance on the United States. Carney's office said the visit aims "to position Canada as a key partner in trade and investment." Although trade between Canada and Turkiye is tiny – Turkiye accounted for less than 0.3 per cent of Canada's total merchandise trade or C$4.34 billion (US$3.09 billion) – bilateral trade has risen by nearly 50 per cent in the past five years.

items.title: Do Malaysians know MA63? Communications Ministry may run a study to find out
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Communications Ministry is considering conducting a dedicated study to gauge public understanding of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and the history of Malaysia’s formation. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said neither the ministry nor its agencies, including the Malaysian Information Department (Japen), had conducted a baseline study for this purpose. “At present, neither RTM nor Japen has conducted a survey to measure public understanding of MA63 and the formation of Malaysia.

items.title: Pay up or go to jail: 43 fined for using other people’s Malaysian ID cards in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 22 — A total of 43 individuals, including three Malaysians, were fined between RM1,000 and RM9,000 by three Magistrates’ Courts here today for using forged identity cards or copies of identity cards belonging to other people. Of the total, 35 were charged with using copies of other people’s identity cards, while the remaining eight were charged with using forged identity cards as personal identification documents. The accused, aged between 18 and 49, comprised three Malaysians and foreign nationals from Indonesia and the Philippines.

items.title: Zetrix AI yet to pay RM314mil in outstanding government revenue, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has yet to make any payment towards the RM314 million in outstanding government revenue, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. He said the suspension of the company's appointment as a Road Transport Department (RTD) collection agent had not disrupted summons payments or other services, which remained accessible through alternative channels, including MyJPJ. "Other services are still available through MyJPJ.

items.title: China slams 'Cold War mentality' after new EU Arctic plan
items.summary: BEIJING: China opposed on Thursday "using Cold War mentality" to stoke conflict over the Arctic, after the European Union linked Beijing's cooperation with Russia in the region to security concerns. The EU unveiled on Tuesday a push to boost Arctic surveillance and expand icebreaker fleets, alluding to China's growing "strategic ambitions... as it deepens its partnership with Russia." Asked about the new EU strategy and calls from foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas to bolster the bloc's defences in the Arctic, China denounced what it called a "Cold War mentality."

items.title: MyEG suspension to continue as RM314m outstanding payment remains unsettled, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said the outstanding payment MyEG Services Bhd (MyEG) owes the government has yet to be settled, following the suspension of the company’s services as a Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection agent earlier this month. MyEG is a digital and e-government services provider that was previously tasked with collecting JPJ-related payments. He said the suspension had not disrupted public access to JPJ services, as motorists could continue using alternative channels, including the MyJPJ application, to access their information and carry out transactions.

items.title: Haze row: Malaysia to take transboundary pollution to Asean meeting in Manila
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia urges Indonesia to take firm and effective action to tackle fires contributing to transboundary haze pollution, which is affecting air quality and public well-being in Malaysia. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia respected its good diplomatic relations with Indonesia but reserved the right to demand appropriate action to ensure its people could enjoy clean air. “Malaysia’s stance is clear.

items.title: 'We are everywhere,' police warn Melaka election candidates, political parties
items.summary: MELAKA: State police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar has warned election candidates, political parties and their supporters not to violate any law during the campaigning period. "Don't come begging for help after you've been detained," he said during a briefing on the 16th Melaka election at the state police headquarters. He said police would ensure that security and public order are maintained throughout the election period.

items.title: TalentCorp business as usual, says HR Ministry, as it lodges reports on alleged interference
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) has lodged several official reports with the authorities over alleged attempts to interfere with an ongoing review and investigation at Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp). In a statement today, the ministry said the alleged interference involved spreading misleading information, influencing individuals within the agency, and diverting attention from matters under scrutiny. It said such actions could undermine the integrity and independence of the review and investigation.

items.title: Norway's wealth fund posts US$30bil loss in Q3
items.summary: OSLO: Norway's US$2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest, reported on Thursday a loss of 278 billion Norwegian crowns (US$29.71 billion) for the third quarter, with a return of minus 0.5 per cent on its global investments. "The fund's return was close to flat, ending slightly negative as rising interest rates led to weaker results on our fixed-income investments," deputy CEO Trond Grande said in a statement. Investing the Norwegian state's revenues from oil and gas production, the fund owns on average 1.5 per cent of all listed companies globally, making it the world's largest single investor.

items.title: 'PN is back': Takiyuddin celebrates court reprieve ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "PN is back!" PN is back! PN is back!"

items.title: Kerian Industrial City targets RM700mil in development value
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerian Industrial City (KIC) is expected to create new opportunities for industrial growth, attract investment and support the expansion of local businesses. Spanning 116.15 hectares with an estimated gross development value of RM700 million, KIC is expected to generate 12,000 jobs, according to Perak State Development Corp (PKNPk). The development will create opportunities for investors, industrial operators, and support service providers to expand their operations in Kerian, accelerating the local economy and contributing to Perak's broader economic growth.

items.title: Indonesia's fire hotspots fall, but wildfire threat remains
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia remains on high alert for wildfires despite a decline in hotspots over the past week, with the sporadic rainfall still not enough to put them out, a disaster agency official said on Thursday, as students on Borneo island staged protests against the government's handling of the crisis. Indonesia has been battling its most intense forest fires in 11 years, with the El Niño weather phenomenon driving up temperatures and leaving the country's vast stretches of forest and peatland more vulnerable to fire. According to data from the EU's Copernicus climate monitoring service, carbon dioxide emissions from Indonesian fires from Oct 15 to Oct 21 reached 14.44 million metric tons, down from 22.22 million tons over the preceding seven days.

items.title: GOF: Illegal entries not confined to Golok River
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: Undocumented migrants are entering Malaysia through various routes, not just the Golok River, prompting the General Operations Force (GOF) to strengthen security along land and sea borders. Internal Security and Public Order Department deputy director Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said this was based on briefings from brigade representatives yesterday. Suzrin said the GOF worked with state police contingents, district police stations, the Marine Police and the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency to detect and respond to border incursions within their respective areas of responsibility.

items.title: Kuching school attack probe ongoing, police to hold press conference on Oct 27
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 22 — Police are gathering and verifying information as investigations into the alleged attack on a female teacher at an international school here yesterday morning continue. According to the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters, the investigation team is carrying out various investigative measures to ensure the accuracy of the information obtained. Yesterday, acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said police received a report of the incident at 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line.

items.title: Foodie Media's net profit soars in first full year as listed firm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Foodie Media Bhd's net profit surged 67.7 per cent to RM15.67 million in its first full financial year as an ACE Market-listed company. For the financial year ended Aug 31, 2026, Foodie Media's revenue rose 49.6 per cent to RM55.49 million from RM37.09 million a year earlier. Its content segment recorded a 28.8 per cent increase in full-year revenue to RM30.4 million, while the creator segment grew 59.8 per cent to RM13.6 million.

items.title: Loke welcomes RM5m Masjid Jamek LRT makeover, wants stations to drive local economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today welcomed a RM5 million beautification project at the Masjid Jamek LRT station, saying the busy interchange should be more than a transit point and help drive economic activity and tourism in the capital. Transport Minister Anthony Loke during the launch of the LRT Masjid Jamek Station Beautification Project in Kuala Lumpur October 22, 2026. Transport Minister Anthony Loke poses for a picture during the launch of the LRT Masjid Jamek Station Beautification Project in Kuala Lumpur October 22, 2026.

items.title: Prabowo's allies turn their backs on troubled free meals scheme
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's big-tent coalition has given him almost unchecked power for two years, but mass food poisoning and graft linked to his flagship free meals programme have emerged as the first major test of their support for the former special forces commander. A member of a third coalition party said their party feared the problems with the scheme would hurt their electoral prospects. Prabowo's Gerindra party has 15 per cent.

items.title: Experts warn Waze location data could expose sensitive movements patterns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's ban on Waze among civil servants has raised questions about the data security risks posed by navigation applications, with experts saying location data could reveal users' daily routines and movements around sensitive facilities. He said research conducted by Peter Gasper in 2020 had demonstrated that Waze could track users' movements under certain conditions. Ridza said allowing Waze to access location data through the "Always" setting could create detailed records of users' daily routines, including their home and workplace locations, frequently travelled routes and visits to sensitive locations.

items.title: SUV driver in fatal Penang hit-and-run surrenders to police
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 23-year-old SUV driver suspected of being involved in a fatal hit-and-run along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway this morning has surrendered to police. Northeast police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the suspect, from Bukit Jambul, surrendered at the Northeast Police Headquarters around 1pm today. He said post-mortem examinations found that the male motorcyclist died from severe head and neck injuries, while his female pillion rider died from severe head injuries.

items.title: 3,435 policemen will be on duty during Melaka election
items.summary: State police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said 1,500 of these would come from other states. He said federal police in Bukit Aman would coordinate the placement of policemen from other states. Speaking to reporters after a briefing on the 16th state election at the state police headquarters, he said police would have a special team which will use technology to strengthen security throughout the election period.

items.title: Viral Porsche driver jailed five days, fined RM10,000 for reckless driving
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The driver of a Porsche Cayenne who went viral for reckless driving and taunting other road users has been sentenced to five days in jail, fined RM10,000 and disqualified from driving for five years. Woo Hong Jiang, 56, an online trader, pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court to reckless and dangerous driving that endangered himself and other road users. Magistrate Nur Natasya Mohtaruddin ordered Woo to begin serving his jail sentence immediately.

items.title: Bandar Kuching MP urges public to stop sharing Kuching school attack videos, warns of copycat effect
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 22 — Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen has urged the public and the media to stop sharing videos of a school violence incident in Kuching, warning that such exposure can lead to a copycat effect. “I appeal to everyone, including the media, to stop sharing videos, images, notes or details of this act,” Dr Yii said in a statement. Dr Yii also pointed to a troubling rise in violent incidents involving students since the killing of a student in Bandar Utama in October 2025.

items.title: DAPSY wants evidence behind Waze security concerns
items.summary: hakimmahari@nst.com.my KUALA LUMPUR: DAP Socialist Youth (DAPSY) wants the government to review its ban on civil servants on Waze, questioning the lack of publicly available evidence that the navigation application poses a threat to national security. It said Waze had been widely used by Malaysians for years, but the public had yet to be presented with sufficient evidence that the application had compromised national security or misused users' data. "Rather than reassuring the public, such a sweeping decision risks generating further questions and undermining public trust," it said.

items.title: Palm oil worker jailed nine months for threatening wife with parang
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A palm oil worker who threatened and chased his wife with a parang after accusing her of having an affair was sentenced to nine months' jail by the magistrate's court here today. Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno imposed the sentence on Ahmad Fairus Mohamed, 42, after he pleaded guilty and after considering the mitigation plea and submissions by the prosecution and defence. According to the charge, Fairus, who has three children, committed criminal intimidation against his 37-year-old wife using a parang at a house in Senggarang here about 8.30am on Oct 18.

items.title: [UPDATED]: Customs seize RM1.33mil in electrical goods, detain warehouse manager
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Customs officers have seized 9,286 electrical appliances worth more than RM1.33 million, including duties and taxes, in a raid on a warehouse in Seri Kembangan, Selangor. A local man in his 60s, who managed the warehouse, was detained to assist investigations into the suspected smuggling of electrical appliances without the required approvals. Kuala Lumpur Customs director Wan Norizan Wan Daud said the raid was conducted at a private warehouse in Bukit Belimbing on Oct 13, following intelligence received from the department's headquarters.

items.title: [UPDATED] High Court grants PN stay on RoS deregistration
items.summary: High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad ruled that RoS' decision to cancel PN's registration on Oct 20 did not render the coalition's application for a stay academic. "Granting the stay would not prejudice the respondents, as PN's political activities could still be monitored by the authorities," he said. In his decision, Azizan said the main issue raised by the respondents was whether PN's stay application had become academic following RoS' decision to cancel its registration before today's hearing.

items.title: Kelantan-Thailand border concertina wire found cut 11 times between March, October
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: The General Operations Force has recorded 11 cases of concertina wire being cut along the Malaysia-Thailand border in Kelantan between March 27 and Oct 12 this year. Internal Security and Public Order Department deputy director (GOF) Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said enforcement action had been taken by the GOF and the respective district police headquarters in connection with the incidents. Suzrin said GOF would continue to update field intelligence in collaboration with the National Security Council and the relevant police contingents on border intrusions involving the cutting of concertina wire.

items.title: Two killed, 8 injured in attack on airport in Saudi oil city Dammam
items.summary: DAMMAM: Two people were killed and eight were injured in an attack on Wednesday evening on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern oil city of Dammam, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Thursday. Those killed were a Saudi citizen and an Indian national, the authority said. Earlier, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the succesful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two on Wednesday.

items.title: RM1,000 aid lands just in time for Deepavali for 400 Negeri Sembilan taxi drivers
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The RM1,000 special financial assistance from the Madani Government has brought relief to more than 400 taxi and hire car drivers in Negeri Sembilan, particularly those celebrating Deepavali, by helping them prepare for the festival, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. He said the aid would help reduce recipients’ financial burden, allowing them to meet the costs of Deepavali preparations and their families’ daily needs. “I promised earlier that the assistance would be delivered before Deepavali.

items.title: Nine charged with being members of ‘Geng Suria’ crime group in Sungai Petani
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 22 — Nine men were charged in the Sessions Court here today with being members of an organised crime group known as the ‘Geng Suria’. They are Thayalan, 28; A. Tana Balan, 30; Muhamad Rizwan Abd Jalil, 28; G. Sritharan, 39; B. Saranraj, 38; A. Simon, 34; G. Suria Prasad (alleged to be the gang leader), 30; A. Suresh, 52; and Kavines, 31. Lawyer S. Sagthiyaraj represented Saranraj and Thayalan, while lawyer Mohammad Naim Kamaruddin represented Sritharan, Simon, and Tana Balan.

items.title: Israeli settlers steal Palestinians' olives as attacks on harvest grow more violent
items.summary: BROUGHT to tears as he recalled Israeli settlers hitting his cherished olive trees with sticks and taking off with the olives, Palestinian Ahmed Salem said he feared being attacked if he tried to intervene. Settlers have intimidated Palestinians harvesting their olives in the occupied West Bank for decades, but this year, not only has violence increased sharply, theft has been widespread, according to Palestinians, Israeli rights groups and the UN. The settlers dumped Salem's olives into sacks and then drove them to a nearby Israeli settler outpost to be pressed into olive oil, the 50-year-old Palestinian told Reuters of the incident around two weeks ago near his village Lubban al-Gharbi.

items.title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in Turkmenistan’s oil and gas sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Malaysia is strengthening its energy partnership with Turkmenistan to unlock new commercial opportunities for companies, particularly in higher-value oil and gas services, technology and specialised engineering, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. “Our companies are ready to work with Turkmenistan partners not only as suppliers, but as long-term collaborators committed to local value creation,” the minister said in his remarks during the opening plenary of the Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan 2026 in Ashgabat. The three-day OGT 2026, which began on Oct 21, brought together 20 Malaysian oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies, including Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), according to a statement by the Economy Ministry today.

items.title: Penang to submit technology centre action plan to MoF next month
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang will submit its action plan and supporting papers for the proposed Penang Technology Financial Centre (PTFC) to the Finance Ministry in November. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said state government officers and the State Finance Department would engage with the ministry on the next steps to advance the proposal. Chow said further discussions with senior ministry officials were expected after the 2027 Budget debate and approval process was completed.

items.title: Penang CM wants clarity on restriction barring civil servants from using Waze
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow wants clarification on the restriction barring civil servants from using Waze, citing the app's role in helping motorists navigate traffic congestion. He said Waze had become a useful tool for drivers across Malaysia, helping them find routes to their destinations more efficiently, particularly amid congestion in cities and towns. "A clearer explanation will help motorists understand the rationale behind the restriction, including whether suitable alternatives are available.

items.title: Malaysia can’t bank on a favourable gas market, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The government is finalising the Natural Gas Roadmap (NGR) to guide the coordinated development of Malaysia’s gas sector in line with national policies and the 13th Malaysia Plan, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said Malaysia must strengthen its gas supply resilience amid global market uncertainty and rising energy demand from advanced manufacturing, data centres and digital industries. “This means supporting the development of domestic gas resources, diversifying sources of imported LNG to complement domestic supply, and ensuring that infrastructure is available to deliver gas to consumers,” he said.

items.title: Zelenskyy open to freezing front lines to end conflict
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he is prepared to freeze the current front lines in a bid to end the conflict, reported German Press Agency (dpa). "Yes, right now, we have to freeze," he said in an interview with United States (US) broadcaster Fox News on Wednesday. Zelenskyy's position is not new.

items.title: Malaysia awaits Nepal's special order to expedite missing-person, death certificates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is awaiting details of Nepal's proposed special order to expedite missing-person and death certificates for victims still unaccounted for following the Aug 26 floods and landslides. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the proposed measure would apply specifically to victims of the disaster and would not cover previous missing-person cases in Nepal. He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had contacted his Nepalese counterpart to discuss the proposed measure.

items.title: On track? Malaysia’s 2030 SDG projection climbs from 49pc to 58pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Malaysia’s projected achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030 has risen to 58 per cent, up from 49 per cent last year, and surpassing the global projection of 35 per cent. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the improvement reflected the country’s progress in advancing the SDG agenda, although further efforts were needed to ensure development benefited all Malaysians. Earlier, Anwar chaired the 2026 National SDG Council meeting, which reviewed Malaysia’s progress in implementing the goals.

items.title: Why your air quality app and the official API don’t match, environment minister explains in Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Air Pollutant Index (API) readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE) remain the government’s official reference for determining air quality and managing haze. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the official API was calculated based on the concentrations of six major pollutants monitored around the clock through 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations nationwide. “Station operations include equipment maintenance, calibration, instrument performance checks and quality assurance procedures to ensure that the data used to calculate the official API are accurate and reliable,” he said during the Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Heading to Kelantan? JKR warns motorists to take care on cracked stretch of Gua Musang road near Yayasan Albarakah
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 22 — The Public Works Department (JKR) in Kelantan has confirmed a landslide along Jalan Lojing-Gua Musang (FT185), near Yayasan Albarakah here yesterday, which caused a 30-metre-long crack in the road surface. Kelantan JKR director Nik Badlihisham Nik Ismail said the landslide at Section 84.15 involved an area stretching 20 metres in length and 30 metres in depth. Meanwhile, Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said no casualties had been reported in the incident.

items.title: Two in three Perakians say their income is enough, but they want more jobs, Institut Darul Ridzuan study shows
items.summary: IDR chief executive Dr Zulqarnain Mohamad said the shift reflected changing public perceptions of current needs, particularly efforts to improve living standards and socioeconomic well-being in the state. He said various state government initiatives, including the Pasar Sejahtera Rakyat programme, had helped address the cost of living and positively impacted people at the grassroots level. Zulqarnain said the study also found that 66.4 per cent of respondents considered their monthly income sufficient, while 58.7 per cent said they could set aside emergency savings.

items.title: No Perikatan, no problem? Political analysts say Opposition faces a tricky Melaka campaign
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The split between PAS and Bersatu following an internal crisis in Perikatan Nasional (PN), which led to the cancellation of the coalition’s registration, could weaken the opposition’s position in the Melaka state election campaign beginning on Oct 31, political analysts say. Ilham Centre research fellow Mujibu Abd Muis said the opposition’s internal turmoil would affect coordination of election strategies, potentially leading to multi-cornered contests, a split in votes and candidates from opposition parties competing against one another. He said PN’s deregistration raised questions about using a common identity and coordinating candidates, prompting PAS and Bersatu to reconsider their strategies for the state election.

items.title: Hit-and-run at 4am: Two dead near Penang Bridge interchange
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 22 — A man and his female companion were killed after their motorcycle was struck by a vehicle in a hit-and-run crash along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway near the Penang Bridge interchange early this morning. Timur Laut District Police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said initial investigations found that the crash occurred at about 4 am as the 22-year-old man and 20-year-old woman were travelling from George Town towards Penang Bridge. Abdul Rozak said their bodies were taken to the Forensic Medicine Department at Penang Hospital for post-mortem.

items.title: Which way to go? TuJu offers a locally-developed navigation app built around Malaysian highways and traffic info
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 22 — As the government encourages Malaysians to consider switching from Waze to locally developed navigation applications, TuJu offers motorists an alternative that combines navigation with live traffic information and highway-related services. Unlike conventional navigation applications that focus primarily on directions and traffic conditions, TuJu also incorporates services specific to Malaysian highways. Who developed TuJu?

items.title: TuJu app to go beyond highways and cover ordinary roads, says digital minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The government is enhancing the locally developed navigation app, TuJu, by expanding its coverage beyond highways to ordinary roads to improve traffic information and user experience, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the move followed public feedback calling for more comprehensive navigation services. Meanwhile, Gobind said the Waze ban applied only to civil servants conducting official government business, citing data security and legal risks.

items.title: Malaysia is ageing fast, but who’s in charge? Advocates call for an ‘anchor ministry’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — As Malaysia rapidly ages, it needs a targeted approach, with a ministry dedicated to older persons and one agency to coordinate all aged care policies. Ezzati Nasir, CEO and founder of Teman Malaysia, which provides care companion services for older persons, said the country’s approach to aged care is currently fragmented across different ministries. “So I feel we have to come together and work on elderly care as one holistic approach and one ministry,” she said.

items.title: High Court rejects bid for closed-door trial in civil suit over Bandar Utama school murder
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The High Court today rejected a bid by the teenager acquitted of murdering his schoolmate Yap Shing Xuen at a Bandar Utama secondary school last year to have the entire civil suit heard in-camera, or in closed-door proceedings. Anand said the court could not determine at this stage which witnesses would testify or the nature of their evidence, adding that the defendants could later apply for specific witnesses to testify in-camera if their evidence was likely to identify the teenager. “The court is cognisant of the Child Act 2001, which restricts the reporting of details identifying a child, and also of the interest of justice and the public interest.

items.title: DAP lawmaker condemns police action against lawyers over sharing of Noorizwan’s custodial death photos
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Jelutong MP RSN Rayer today criticised the police for opening an investigation against lawyers representing Noorizwan Zulkefly, the 42-year-old who died while in police custody. Rayer suggested the investigation was a form of intimidation, as he defended their right to share the photos of Noorizwan’s body that his family’s lawyers alleged showed signs of blunt force trauma, including broken ribs and severe head and spinal injuries. “I take seriously the police’s statement that the lawyers who shared those photos are being subject to investigation.

items.title: Last phone pings of 54 missing Malaysians traced to Nepal glacial flood site, foreign minister tells Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The last signals emitted from the mobile phones of the missing Malaysians in Nepal were traced directly to the location hit by a “glacial tsunami”, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan told the Dewan Rakyat. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had requested an executive order from Nepal’s Prime Minister to shorten the waiting period for issuing death certificates in disaster cases, Mohamad told Parliament. The Nepalese government agreed to issue an executive order reducing the process to 45 days, according to the minister.

items.title: Govt urges Malaysians to uninstall Waze over Israeli data laws, stops short of blanket ban
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 22 — The government has urged Malaysians to uninstall Waze over concerns that users’ personal and movement data could fall under Israeli jurisdiction. National Security Council director-general for National Security Raja Datuk Nushirwan Zainal Abidin, however, said there will not be a blanket ban issued to preserve individual freedom of choice. He said the government would not compromise on the use of Malaysians’ data and the sovereignty of national information.
